name: Time of supply — services
definition: The time of supply of services is the date fixed by s.13 at which the liability to pay tax on services arises. Under forward charge it is the earliest of three dates: where the invoice is issued within the period prescribed under s.31, the earlier of the invoice date and the date of receipt of payment; where it is not, the earlier of the date of provision of service and the date of receipt of payment; and, where neither applies, the date the recipient shows the receipt of services in his books. Under reverse charge it is the earlier of the date of payment in the recipient's records and the date immediately following sixty days from the date of issue of invoice.
why_it_exists: It fixes WHEN the GST liability on a service arises, and therefore its return period. s.13(1) ties the liability itself to this date. The rule differs from goods in three ways that matter — earliest of THREE limbs rather than earlier of two, a timeliness test on the invoice, and a SIXTY-day reverse-charge clock. This is NOT the accounting revenue recognition date; the two determinations are separate and can fall in different periods.
inputs: whether tax is payable on forward charge or reverse charge
the date of issue of invoice, and whether it was issued within the period prescribed under s.31
the date of provision of the service
the date of receipt of payment — the supplier's book entry date and bank credit date
the date the recipient showed receipt of the services in his books
for reverse charge: the recipient's book entry and bank debit dates, and the invoice date
whether supplier and recipient are associated enterprises, and whether the supplier is located outside India
outputs: a single date — the time of supply of the services
a separate date for any addition to value under s.13(6)
or an escalation, where a limb cannot be evaluated on the evidence held
preconditions: the transaction is a supply under s.7 (GST-SUPPLY-SCOPE)
it is classified as a supply of SERVICES — if it is a supply of goods, s.12 governs instead
there is NO change in the rate of tax — s.14 displaces s.13 if there is (GST-TIME-RATE-CHANGE-001)
exceptions: a change in the rate of tax — s.14 applies notwithstanding s.13 (GST-TIME-RATE-CHANGE-001)
excess received up to one thousand rupees — s.13(2) proviso, at the supplier's option (GST-TIME-SERVICES-005)
associated enterprises with the supplier located outside India — s.13(3) second proviso (GST-TIME-SERVICES-009)
additions to value by interest, late fee or penalty — s.13(6) (GST-TIME-SERVICES-012)

common_mistakes: applying the goods rule — s.12(2) is EARLIER of two limbs, s.13(2) is EARLIEST of three
assuming a late invoice pushes the tax point forward — s.13(2)(b) moves it BACK to the date the service was provided
using the THIRTY-day reverse-charge clock from s.12(3)(c) — s.13(3)(b) is SIXTY days
reading s.13(2)(c) as a free alternative — it applies only where (a) and (b) do not
using the recipient's book date for the s.13(2) receipt of payment — Explanation (ii) names the SUPPLIER's books
treating the time of supply as the accounting revenue recognition date — separate determinations, potentially different periods

evidence_required: the tax invoice, with its date of issue
evidence of the date the service was provided
proof of the date payment was received — the supplier's book entry and the bank credit
for s.13(2)(c): the recipient's books showing receipt of the services
for reverse charge: the recipient's book entry and bank debit dates
confidence_factors: weak when the s.31 prescribed period is unknown, because the switch between s.13(2)(a) and s.13(2)(b) turns entirely on it
weak when the date of provision of service is not evidenced — for a late invoice, that date IS the tax point
weak when it is unclear whether the supply is on reverse charge
zero when a change in the rate of tax is in play — s.14 displaces this concept and its limbs are not extracted
validation_checks: the chosen date is the EARLIEST of the applicable limbs
the invoice-timeliness test under s.31 is applied before choosing between s.13(2)(a) and s.13(2)(b)
the reverse-charge clock used is SIXTY days, not thirty
the receipt-of-payment date under s.13(2) is taken from the SUPPLIER's records
the time of supply is recorded separately from any accounting revenue recognition date
examples: service provided on the 2nd, invoice issued late on the 40th, payment received on the 50th — s.13(2)(b) applies and the time of supply is the 2nd, the earlier of provision and payment
reverse charge, invoice issued on the 1st, payment entered in the recipient's books on the 90th — the sixty-day limb gives the 62nd, which is earlier and governs
counterexamples: an advance received for a service not yet performed — no revenue is recognised under AS-9, yet the receipt of payment is a limb of s.13(2), so a GST time of supply can arise while the accounting books show none
